benchmarks.claim: Dollars attributed to a Native entity by hand that the flag never sees
benchmarks.cicd_figure: not sized — CICD calls its own dataset a "lower-bound estimate"
benchmarks.cedar_basis: prime_contracts.csv, attributed_flag=1, total_obligations, set-aside forward-filled to award level on (contract_number, awardee_uei)
benchmarks.explanation: $140.00B of the $244.77B Cedar attributes to a Native entity — 57.2% of it, on 565,364 rows — sits on awards carrying NO Native set-aside of any kind. A flag-based method recovers the complement, $104.76B. This is the size of the shortfall CICD named and never measured, and it is a FLOOR: 8(a) is open to non-Native firms, so the set-aside instrument used here is more generous than the business-type self-certification flag CICD actually uses.

benchmarks.claim: Native ENTITIES invisible to the flag
benchmarks.cicd_figure: FPDS flags found 241 contracting tribes against 588 recognized entities (AGENTS.md, BGOV audit)
benchmarks.cedar_basis: distinct tribe_id on attributed rows, vs those with >=1 award-filled Native-preference row
benchmarks.explanation: Cedar attributes prime obligations to 498 entities. Only 303 of them ever appear on a Native-preference award. 195 entities — 39.16% of the attributed universe, holding $1.18B — are invisible to any flag-based discovery method. The dollar figure is small and the ENTITY figure is the finding: a directory built from flags is missing two entities in five.

benchmarks.claim: Native-owned FIRMS invisible to the flag
benchmarks.cedar_basis: distinct awardee_uei on attributed rows vs those with >=1 award-filled Native-preference row
benchmarks.explanation: 1,362 of 3,215 attributed awardee firms (42.36%) never carry a Native set-aside on any row, holding $27.61B. These are firms Cedar has already tied to a Native owner; a flag-based build would not have found them to attribute.

benchmarks.claim: Hand-ruled individually-Native firms with ZERO self-certification
benchmarks.cicd_figure: n/a — CICD's method cannot reach this class
benchmarks.explanation: 22 of 40 firms the owner ruled individually Native-owned, from the firms' own statements, carry no Native self-certification on a single contract row — $212.5M. The largest, Frontier Electronic Systems, is 998 rows and $204.2M with no flag at all. This is a person finding what the instrument cannot. CAUTION, from the build log: the sample is Cherokee-heavy (31 of 45 rulings came from one do-file pass), so the DIRECTION of the undercount is established and its MAGNITUDE across Indian Country is not.

benchmarks.claim: Why the true business-type flag cannot be used to size this
benchmarks.cicd_figure: USAspending business-type flags: tribally owned / ANC-owned / NHO-owned
benchmarks.explanation: The only file in this corpus carrying the true business-type flags was EXTRACTED BY those flags, so 98.95% of its rows are flagged by construction. A flag-defined universe cannot measure what the flag misses. The corpus-wide instrument is therefore the set-aside family in prime_contracts.csv, and every undercount figure above is typed METHOD for that reason. Loading the two INDIVIDUAL_NATIVE_OWNED SAM variants does not fix this — they are flag-defined too.

benchmarks.claim: Count of tribal gaming facilities
benchmarks.cicd_figure: NIGC FY2025: 545 operations, 246 tribes, 29 states, $46.2B GGR (via TBN/CDC Gaming, 2026-07-21). CRS IF12527, Sept 2024: 532 establishments, 243 tribes, $43.9B
benchmarks.explanation: DIFFERENT UNIVERSE AND DIFFERENT PERIOD. NIGC's 545 counts operations licensed in ONE fiscal year. Cedar's 784 is a HISTORICAL universe assembled from three rosters spanning the whole tribal gaming era, and it includes closed properties, non-casino gaming locations and rows flagged as possible duplicates. See GAMING-02 for the bridge. Publishing 784 against 545 without it reads as an error, not as broader coverage.

benchmarks.claim: THE BRIDGE — what the 784 rows are
benchmarks.cicd_figure: NIGC 545 operations (FY2025) · 532 establishments (Sept 2024, CRS IF12527) · 497 distinct locations on NIGC's own public map (510 rows, measured from the retrieved roster)
benchmarks.cedar_basis: gaming_facilities.csv composition + gaming_nigc_roster_link.csv + the retrieved NIGC roster
benchmarks.explanation: **The bridge, in one line: 784 rows = 449 `property_status = current` + 1 `approved` + 334 with NO status recorded.** Of the blank-status rows, 164 are `votingpatterns_only_no_exact_casino_city_match` and every one of those carries `duplicate_risk = 1` — they are candidate duplicates of a vendor row, not confirmed additional properties. 148 rows carry a close date at all. 453 rows link to NIGC's own roster at `igra_coverage_status = VERIFIED_NIGC_OPERATION` — 91.15% of the 497 distinct locations NIGC itself publishes; the unmatched remainder is queued as possible duplicates, never asserted as new properties. 574 rows are independently evidenced (an independently-minted id or an NIGC link — Casino City establishes nothing publishable). **THE COMPARABLE OPERATING FIGURE IS 449, WHICH IS BELOW NIGC'S 545 AND BELOW ITS 532** — Cedar UNDERCOUNTS operating facilities and OVERCOUNTS the historical universe, which is the opposite of how an unbridged 784 reads. Note also that NIGC's own public map (497) sits below NIGC's own press count (545): the federal regulator disagrees with itself by ~48 locations. Lead with 449 current or 574 independently evidenced, name the NIGC baseline, and say what the rest are. *(Minor: this harness de-duplicates the NIGC roster on lower-cased name + upper-cased state and gets 497; `docs/GAMING_UNIVERSE_REBUILD_2026-08-26.md` reports 496 from script 157's own normalisation. One location, a normalisation difference, recorded rather than silently reconciled.)*

benchmarks.claim: Rows that are BOTH `current` AND carry a close date
benchmarks.cedar_basis: gaming_facilities.csv, property_status in (current, approved) AND close_date populated
benchmarks.explanation: 115 rows read as a contradiction and are not one, but a reader will call it one. `property_status = current` is the vendor's status LITERAL AT `property_status_observed_date`, and `close_date` is the vendor's *first* close date — so a property that closed and reopened carries both (Casino Morongo: close 2010-12-05, observed Open 2023). The column semantics must ship in the codebook beside these rows. Net: 335 rows are current with no close date at all.

benchmarks.claim: Federal contract revenue to Native entities, last decade (2016-2025)
benchmarks.cedar_basis: prime_contracts.csv FY2016-25 total_obligations + subawards.csv FY2016-25 subaward_amount (duplicate_status=primary)
benchmarks.explanation: Like-for-like: $173.52B prime + $17.20B sub = $190.72B against CICD's ~$200B, a -4.6% difference. FOUR DEFINITIONAL DIFFERENCES remain and all four must travel with any published comparison: (a) CEDAR'S SUBAWARD LAYER IS INCOMPLETE — FY2021-24 hold 173/89/120/166 rows against ~5,000/yr either side, because the USAspending bulk download service failed service-wide for those years; the sub figure is a known floor. (b) CICD reports action/calendar year, Cedar fiscal year. (c) Cedar's figure is nominal; CICD's decade figure is nominal but its 1981-2021 figure is 2021 dollars — never compare across those two. (d) CICD's recent series is flag-based, Cedar's is the identifier ledger; on the ATTRIBUTED basis Cedar reads $145.84B + sub. Given (a) alone would close most of the remaining gap, these two numbers agree.

benchmarks.claim: 2025 award total to Native entities, prime + sub
benchmarks.explanation: $21.24B against $26.6B, -20.2%. Three named differences. (a) CALENDAR vs FISCAL YEAR: CICD's "2025" is action-date calendar 2025; Cedar's is FY2025 (2024-10-01 to 2025-09-30), and the quarter of difference falls in a rising series. (b) RETRIEVAL DATE: CICD retrieved 2026-08-04, Cedar's FY2025 rows come from the 20260806 archive vintage — USAspending back-fills obligations for months after year-end, so the LATER retrieval is the larger. (c) Cedar's FY2023-26 rows were pulled FILTERED to known Native identifiers rather than full-universe, so FY2025 is 100% attributed BY CONSTRUCTION and any firm not already in the identifier ledger is absent from it entirely. (c) is the one that could hide a real shortfall and it is the reason this row is DEFINITIONAL rather than CORROBORATED.

benchmarks.claim: Cedar Press lifetime prime total
benchmarks.explanation: NOT COMPARABLE AS STATED and must never be printed beside $202B without this line. Cedar: $310.01B nominal, FY2000-2026, prime only. CICD: $202B in 2021 dollars, 1981-2021, prime + sub. Three of the four axes differ (period, deflation, prime/sub). Cedar holds NO pre-FY2000 rows, so the first nineteen years of CICD's window are simply absent. Cedar's FY2000-2021 attributed figure is $164.88B, nominal.

benchmarks.claim: DoD share of Native-entity contract revenue, 2000-2021
benchmarks.cedar_basis: prime_contracts.csv, attributed rows FY2000-2021, defense=1 share of total_obligations
benchmarks.explanation: 63.76% against CICD's 67.6% on the same window — a -3.84pt gap, just outside this file's 5% band. **A hypothesis was tested and killed rather than asserted.** Cedar's `defense` flag is `funding_agency == 'Dept Of Defense'` and excludes rows filed under 'U.S. Army Corps Of Engineers - Civil Program Financing Only'; adding those rows ($0.51B) moves the share only to 64.07%, so the exclusion accounts for 0.31pt of 3.84pt. The entity-mix explanation runs the WRONG WAY: Cedar's population includes NHOs, which CICD reports at >90% DoD, so including them should RAISE Cedar's share, not lower it. **The residual ~3.5pt is unaccounted.** Severity LOW — this is a near-agreement between two independent 22-year builds and the most likely remaining cause is that the two attributed populations of dollars are not the same set. TO SETTLE IT: recompute both shares on an entity set present in both builds.

benchmarks.claim: Federally recognized tribes contracting as of 2021
benchmarks.cicd_figure: ~150 tribes involved with federal contracting as of 2021
benchmarks.cedar_basis: prime_contracts.csv, distinct tribe_id with the TRBF- NEID prefix on attributed FY2021 rows
benchmarks.cedar_display: 173 federally recognized tribes (of 287 entities of all classes)
benchmarks.explanation: **The like-for-like is 173, not 287.** The unrestricted FY2021 count of 287 is entities of ALL classes — restricting to the NEID `TRBF-` prefix (federally recognized tribe) gives 173, against CICD's ~150. Full FY2021 mix: AKNF 36, ANRC 12, ANVC 41, CNSF 6, CNSS 1, NHO 4, SGVF 3, TRBF 173, TRBS 11. Cedar finds 23 more contracting tribes than the flag-based method, +15% — **the same direction and roughly the same magnitude as the entity-level undercount in UNDERCOUNT-02**, which is what makes this a corroboration of the undercount finding rather than a disagreement about tribes. Setting 287 against 150 would have been a category error; it is recorded here so nobody does it.

benchmarks.claim: Share of Native-prime subcontracts going to non-Native firms
benchmarks.cedar_basis: subawards.csv, duplicate_status=primary, prime_native_tribe_id populated, sub_native_tribe_id blank
benchmarks.explanation: 95.52% against CICD's 95.2%, a +0.3pt gap on a figure neither build tuned. Cedar's is all subawards under a Native prime; CICD's is small-business subs only, 2015-2023. LOW priority by owner instruction — the non-Native comparison is deferred — but it was one pass over 63,548 rows and it corroborates, so it is recorded. Note it is NOT the 92.9% figure: that is a different window and a different denominator.

benchmarks.claim: Contracts in the hand-adjudicated dataset
benchmarks.cedar_basis: prime_contracts.csv, attributed FY2000-2021 rows, three candidate award keys
benchmarks.explanation: **No Cedar award key reproduces 50,167, and the grain hypothesis was tested rather than assumed.** Three candidate keys on attributed FY2000-2021 rows: parent PIID 15,985, PIID 173,716, PIID+UEI 221,058. CICD's 50,167 sits BETWEEN the first two and matches none. Period does not explain it either — CICD's window is 1981-2021 and Cedar's is FY2000-2021, so CICD covers nineteen MORE years and still reports a smaller number. **CICD does not state its contract key**, so the difference cannot currently be resolved from either side's published description. Severity MEDIUM: it does not touch a dollar figure, but any "contracts" count Cedar publishes will be compared to 50,167 and needs its key stated in the same sentence. TO SETTLE IT: ask what BGOV's contract grain was — award, transaction, or award-year-vendor.

benchmarks.claim: Native share of ALL federal contract dollars
benchmarks.explanation: Requires a denominator of ALL federal contracting, which Cedar does not hold — prime_contracts.csv is a Native-filtered pull, not a full-universe extract. The denominator would have to come from a fresh USAspending pull. Deprioritised by the owner: comparison to non-Native entities is not a current priority.

benchmarks.claim: Contracting vs gaming growth rates
benchmarks.explanation: Cedar holds NO prime contract rows before FY2000, so the 1988 base year does not exist in this corpus and an annualised rate over 1988-2021 cannot be computed. Recomputing it over FY2000-2021 would be a different statistic wearing the same label. Deferred.

benchmarks.claim: Share of revenue earned off tribal lands
benchmarks.explanation: prime_contracts.csv carries place-of-performance CITY and STATE but no tribal-land geography, and no AIANNH-code join exists on this file. Computing it means intersecting place of performance against Census AIANNH areas — real work, not a query. NOT attempted.

benchmarks.claim: 8(a) sole-source share, >50% to ~35%
benchmarks.explanation: UNBLOCKED 2026-08-26, STILL NOT COMPUTED HERE. It was blocked by INTERNAL-05: `extent_competed` carried TWO VOCABULARIES, so any filter on it selected a source vintage and a naive computation read 0.9% then 5.3% — a measurement of the vintage boundary and nothing else. `extent_competed_normalized` now exists and makes the series computable (`code/207_normalize_extent_competed.py`, crosswalk in `code/cedar_extent_competed.py`, write-up in `docs/EXTENT_COMPETED_CROSSWALK.md`). It is NOT computed here because the numerator is a DEFINITIONAL choice that has to be stated, not looked up: FAR Part 6 codes B and C are the non-competitive exceptions, F/G are Simplified Acquisition Procedures under FAR Part 13 and are not a Part 6 competition at all, and CDO/NDO are fair-opportunity on delivery orders under FAR 16.505(b)(1). Whoever publishes this must say which of the nine categories they counted as sole source.

benchmarks.claim: NEED — establishments and tribes
benchmarks.cicd_figure: 5,559 establishments owned by 344 federally recognized tribes (CICD NEED v2025Q4)
benchmarks.explanation: NEED is an ESTABLISHMENT universe built from tribes' own websites with NETS attributes. Cedar's spine is an ENTITY universe (1,310) with a commercial-identifier ledger. The two count different objects and no arithmetic bridges them. Not a delta; a scope difference. Recorded so nobody sets 1,310 against 5,559.

benchmarks.claim: prime_contracts.csv headline row count and total
benchmarks.explanation: Every headline figure in START_HERE.md reproduces exactly from the file as of this run's mtime stamp.

benchmarks.claim: The 79.0% attribution rate is a BLEND of two populations
benchmarks.explanation: All 209,495 FY2023-FY2026 rows are attributed_flag = 1 because the archive backfill was pulled FILTERED to Cedar's known identifiers rather than full-universe. FY2000-2022 came from the BGOV-filtered .dta and carries a mixed rate (FY2000 48%, FY2021 78%). So 79.0% is a blend over two differently-constructed populations and is NOT a quality measure of any single year. It also means a Native firm not already in the ledger is absent from FY2023-26 entirely — the recent years cannot discover anything new.

benchmarks.claim: Summing subawards past `duplicate_status` double-counts
benchmarks.explanation: 14,637 rows are `exact_repeat_within_source` and 846 are `superseded_by_primary_source`. Summing all 63,548 rows returns $39.43B against a true $25.77B — a 53% inflation. `duplicate_status = 'primary'` is mandatory on every subaward money figure and belongs in cedar_domain beside SUM_COLUMNS.

benchmarks.claim: The forbidden sums, computed on purpose
benchmarks.cedar_display: total_award_value sums to $5.63T; total_obligations_real2025 sums to $385.0B; TRUE figure is $310.01B
benchmarks.explanation: Recorded so a phantom is recognisable by its magnitude. `total_award_value` is in MAX_PER_AWARD_COLUMNS — it is the award ceiling restated on every transaction row of that award, and summing it is a category error, not an overcount. `total_obligations_real2025` is a RESTATEMENT of a column already summed; it looks plausible, which makes it the more dangerous of the two. The multi-trillion phantom recorded earlier today has the shape of the total_award_value sum. Neither figure is ever a dollar total of anything.

benchmarks.claim: `extent_competed` carries two vocabularies in one column
benchmarks.cedar_display: 355,644 single-letter + 4,265 multi-letter FPDS codes · 839,028 rendered labels · 9,420 blank · 9,411 literal `nan` · 0 undefined by the dictionary — NORMALISED into `extent_competed_normalized`
benchmarks.explanation: **RESOLVED 2026-08-26 — and the original diagnosis above was WRONG ABOUT WHICH ERA.** The finding itself stands: one column holds raw FPDS codes on some rows and rendered description tags on others, so any filter on it selects a SOURCE VINTAGE rather than a competition status — the same failure shape as the set-aside definition change that nearly corrupted the flagship statistic. But this row previously said the codes came from 'BGOV-era rows'. Measured: BGOV rows (`master prime file.dta`) are 100% LABELS plus 9,420 blanks and carry ZERO codes. **The seam is at the FY2016/FY2017 boundary INSIDE the USAspending award archive** — the FY2008-FY2016 monthly files put the code in the description-tag column and FY2017+ put the label there — and it is confirmed in the raw extracts, so it is UPSTREAM of Cedar, not a defect in 40_build_prime_contracts.py or 114_pull_prime_archive.py. FIXED by `code/207_normalize_extent_competed.py`, which adds `extent_competed_normalized` and `extent_competed_normalized_basis` and leaves `extent_competed` untouched as evidence. The crosswalk is quoted VERBATIM in `code/cedar_extent_competed.py` from DAIMS-DEC v2.2 (2022-06-03), https://files.usaspending.gov/docs/Data_Dictionary_Crosswalk.xlsx — it was not inferred from our data. Every one of the 20 distinct tokens in the file is accounted for; the only undefined one is the literal `nan`, which is a null and normalises to NOT_REPORTED, never to a competition status. The two vocabularies RECONCILE once mapped: FY2016 (codes) against FY2017 (labels), largest single-category share gap 1.86 pp. **Caveat that survives the fix:** this is an in-place enricher, so a rebuild of prime_contracts.csv reverts it and 207 must be re-run. See `docs/EXTENT_COMPETED_CROSSWALK.md`, which also audits every other categorical column on this file for the same seam.

benchmarks.claim: `reported_native_preference` is NOT a Native identifier
benchmarks.cedar_basis: prime_contracts.csv: reported_native_preference vs Buy Indian + Indian Business only
benchmarks.explanation: `reported_native_preference` is the union of 8(a), Buy Indian and Indian Business. **8(a) is open to non-Native firms**, so this column identifies a PREFERENCE CHANNEL, never Native ownership. The two genuinely Native-specific set-asides total $1.92B — 0.78% of attributed dollars, meaning $243.56B of attributed obligations carry no Native-specific set-aside at all. Anyone reading this column as a Native flag will over-report in one direction and under-report in the other.

benchmarks.claim: Set-aside must be forward-filled to award level before any share is computed
benchmarks.cedar_basis: prime_contracts.csv, row-level vs award-filled native preference
benchmarks.explanation: The fill moves $9.24B and 29,482 rows. A set-aside is a property of the AWARD, not of each modification; the archive reports it per transaction and leaves it blank on ~56% of rows while the BGOV .dta carries the award's value on every row. Read row-level, a preference share is partly a measurement of WHICH SOURCE the row came from. Every flag figure in this file is award-filled. Quoting a row-level share is the defect AGENTS.md records as nearly corrupting the flagship statistic.

largest_flagless.name: Cherokee Joint Venture Limited Liability Company

sam_flags.note: This file carries the TRUE USAspending/SAM business-type flags (flag_tribally_owned_firm, flag_alaskan_native_corporation_owned, flag_native_hawaiian_org_owned, flag_american_indian_owned). It cannot be used to size the undercount: the extract was QUERIED BY the flag, so its near-100% flagged share is a property of the query. A flag-defined universe can never measure what the flag misses. Only the TRIBAL variant is loaded; the two INDIVIDUAL_NATIVE_OWNED variants are still generating.
